subject: sms-casual
content: Ill be at yours in about 3 mins but look out for me
clues: typo 'Ill' with no apostrophe; short and practical, like a real quick text
explanation: Real people text in a hurry: missing apostrophes and half sentences are a good sign of a human.

subject: sms-casual
content: I walked an hour 2 c u! doesnt that show I care y wont u believe im serious?
clues: '2 c u' and 'y wont u' text-speak; emotional and a bit messy
explanation: Strong, messy feelings and text-speak like '2 c u' are typical of real people, not polished AI.

subject: sms-casual
content: Okay. No no, just shining on. That was meant to be signing, but that sounds better.
clues: jokes about its own autocorrect typo; quirky humour
explanation: People laugh at their own typos. AI rarely makes a typo and then jokes about it.

subject: sms-casual
content: Quite lor. But dun tell him wait he get complacent...
clues: Singlish 'lor' and 'dun'; refers to someone without explaining who
explanation: Local slang and references only the friend would understand are hard for AI to fake.

subject: sms-casual
content: Garbage bags, eggs, jam, bread, hannaford wheat chex
clues: just a shopping list; specific shop brand
explanation: A bare list with no greeting is how people really text family. AI tends to add friendly sentences around it.

subject: sms-casual
content: Hmm...Bad news...Hype park plaza $700 studio taken...Only left 2 bedrm-$900...
clues: ellipses everywhere; specific prices and place
explanation: Specific, slightly chaotic details (prices, a plaza name, lots of '...') point to a real person.

subject: sms-casual
content: Printer is cool. I mean groovy. Wine is groovying
clues: silly made-up word 'groovying'; no context
explanation: Odd little jokes that only make sense in the moment are very human.

subject: sms-casual
content: Will it help if we propose going back again tomorrow
clues: neutral, correct sentence; could be anyone
explanation: Some real messages are plain and tidy. When there are no clues, it's fine to be unsure.

subject: sms-casual
content: Having lunch:)you are not in online?why?
clues: no spaces after punctuation; ':)' squeezed in
explanation: Rushed punctuation like 'lunch:)you' is a human habit. AI writes neatly spaced sentences.

subject: sms-casual
content: It's fine, imma get a drink or somethin. Want me to come find you?
clues: 'imma' and 'somethin'; relaxed slang
explanation: Casual slang and dropped letters are a sign of a real person typing fast.

subject: sms-casual
content: Boo I'm on my way to my moms. She's making tortilla soup. Yummmm
clues: 'Boo' and 'Yummmm' with extra letters
explanation: Stretched words like 'Yummmm' are how people show feelings in texts.

subject: sms-casual
content: Just finished eating. Got u a plate. NOT leftovers this time.
clues: inside joke 'NOT leftovers this time'
explanation: The capital 'NOT' points to a shared history only these two people know about.

subject: sms-casual
content: I shall book chez jules for half eight, if that's ok with you?
clues: British 'half eight'; specific restaurant; polite question
explanation: Polite and well written, but very specific plans like 'half eight' at a named place feel real.

subject: sms-casual
content: Tee hee. Off to lecture, cheery bye bye.
clues: 'Tee hee' and 'cheery bye bye'; playful
explanation: Playful sign-offs like 'cheery bye bye' are personal quirks that AI doesn't usually copy.

subject: sms-casual
content: Oh and by the way you do have more food in your fridge! Want to go out for a meal tonight?
clues: complete, friendly sentences with an exclamation mark
explanation: This one reads almost like AI because it's tidy, but it's real. Neat writing alone doesn't prove AI.

subject: prize
content: URGENT! Your Mobile number has been awarded a <UKP>2000 prize GUARANTEED. Call 09061790125 from landline. Claim 3030. Valid 12hrs only 150ppm
clues: URGENT in capitals; prize you never entered; premium 09 number
explanation: You can't win a prize you never entered. 'URGENT' plus 'call now' is a classic scam.

subject: prize
content: You have won a Nokia 7250i. This is what you get when you win our FREE auction. To take part send Nokia to 86021 now. HG/Suite342/2Lands Row/W1JHL 16+
clues: 'You have won'; asks you to text a short code
explanation: Winning something you never took part in is a red flag. Texting short codes can cost money.

subject: phone-plan
content: 4mths half price Orange line rental & latest camera phones 4 FREE. Had your phone 11mths+? Call MobilesDirect free on 08000938767 to update now! or2stoptxt T&Cs
clues: too-good-to-be-true deal; pressure to call
explanation: Unasked-for offers of free phones push you to call. Contact your provider through its official app instead.

subject: prize
content: Txt: CALL to No: 86888 & claim your reward of 3 hours talk time to use from your phone now! Subscribe6GBP/mnth inc 3hrs 16 stop?txtStop www.gamb.tv
clues: 'claim your reward'; small print says you subscribe for 6GBP a month
explanation: Read the small print: 'Subscribe 6GBP/mnth' means the 'reward' costs you money every month.

subject: prize
content: Urgent! Please call 09061213237 from landline. £5000 cash or a luxury 4* Canary Islands Holiday await collection. T&Cs SAE PO Box 177. M227XY. 150ppm. 16+
clues: 'Urgent!'; £5000 cash or holiday; premium 09 number
explanation: Huge prizes and urgency are the oldest scam trick. Real companies don't hand out cash by text.

subject: phone-plan
content: December only! Had your mobile 11mths+? You are entitled to update to the latest colour camera mobile for Free! Call The Mobile Update Co FREE on 08002986906
clues: 'December only!' time pressure; free upgrade offer
explanation: Time pressure like 'December only!' is meant to stop you thinking. Check with your provider directly.

subject: prize
content: Ur balance is now £600. Next question: Complete the landmark, Big, A. Bob, B. Barry or C. Ben ?. Text A, B or C to 83738. Good luck!
clues: fake 'balance' of £600; quiz that charges per text
explanation: A pretend balance and an easy quiz keep you texting a paid number. The money is never real.

subject: travel
content: "For the most sparkling shopping breaks from 45 per person; call 0121 2025050 or visit www.shortbreaks.org.uk"
clues: looks like an ad; unknown website and phone number
explanation: Unsolicited deals pointing to unknown sites are spam. Search the company yourself before you call.

subject: sms-casual
content: Hey! Just wanted to check in and see how your day is going. Let me know if you'd like to grab dinner later this week — I'm free Thursday or Friday! 😊
clues: perfect punctuation and an em dash; generic 'check in' opener; neatly placed emoji
explanation: AI texts often sound like a friendly template: tidy, upbeat and with no personal detail.

subject: sms-casual
content: Good morning! I hope you slept well. Don't forget to drink plenty of water and take some time for yourself today. You've got this! 💪
clues: sounds like a wellness poster; every sentence is encouragement
explanation: Real friends rarely send a list of wellness tips. Motivational filler is a common AI habit.

subject: sms-casual
content: Thanks so much for having us over last night! The food was absolutely delicious and we had such a wonderful time. Let's do it again soon!
clues: 'absolutely delicious', 'wonderful time'; nothing specific about the evening
explanation: Lots of praise but no details (which dish? what happened?) is a sign of AI writing.

subject: sms-casual
content: Running a few minutes late, apologies for the inconvenience! I should be there in approximately 10 minutes.
clues: 'apologies for the inconvenience' and 'approximately' are too formal for a friend
explanation: Office-style phrases like 'apologies for the inconvenience' feel odd between friends.

subject: sms-casual
content: Just picked up groceries! Got eggs, bread, milk, and some fresh veggies. Is there anything else you need while I'm out?
clues: a complete, tidy list with an Oxford comma; cheerful exclamation
explanation: Compare it with a real shopping text: people just list items. AI wraps them in polite sentences.

subject: sms-casual
content: Happy birthday!! 🎉 I hope your day is filled with joy, laughter, and everything that makes you smile. Can't wait to celebrate with you!
clues: card-style wish 'filled with joy, laughter, and...'; list of three
explanation: Birthday wishes in a neat list of three sound like a greeting card, a typical AI pattern.

subject: sms-casual
content: Oh no, I'm so sorry to hear that! That sounds really frustrating. Is there anything I can do to help? I'm here if you need to talk.
clues: says all the 'right' supportive things in order; no reference to what happened
explanation: AI is good at sounding caring in general, but it doesn't mention the actual problem.

subject: sms-casual
content: omg yes!! that movie was so good, the ending totally caught me off guard. we should def watch the sequel together
clues: uses casual style but still fully correct grammar; no movie name
explanation: Even when AI writes casually, it often avoids naming specifics. Who forgets to say which film?

subject: sms-casual
content: Heading to the gym now, then I'll swing by the store. Want me to pick anything up for dinner?
clues: plain and useful; slightly too smooth
explanation: This could easily be human. Tidy, complete plans are only a weak clue for AI.

subject: sms-casual
content: haha that's hilarious 😂 can't believe he actually said that to the teacher
clues: short and casual; laughs at something without any detail
explanation: Hard one. Short reactions are easy for AI to imitate. Look for details only a real friend would know.

subject: sms-casual
content: Sorry, I missed your call! Was in a meeting. Can I call you back in about 20 mins?
clues: realistic and short; 'mins' looks casual
explanation: AI can write very normal messages. When nothing stands out, it's genuinely hard to tell.

subject: sms-casual
content: ugh traffic is awful today, stuck on the ring road. save me a seat?
clues: realistic complaint; lowercase on purpose
explanation: AI can copy lowercase, casual texting. Be careful about trusting style alone.

subject: sms-casual
content: Did you end up finding your keys? I swear they were on the kitchen counter this morning
clues: follows up on something earlier; missing full stop
explanation: Very hard: it refers to earlier events and leaves out the full stop, just like a person would.

subject: sms-casual
content: k see u at 7. bring the charger pls mine died
clues: very short, abbreviations, no emoji
explanation: When AI is told to 'text like a person', it can be almost impossible to spot. That's why we check sources, not just style.

subject: sms-casual
content: mum says dinner's at 6 not 7, dont be late again lol
clues: family detail, 'again lol', missing apostrophe
explanation: Even small 'human' mistakes can be generated. Don't rely on one clue; think about who is likely to send it.

subject: delivery
content: ParcelPost: Your package could not be delivered due to an unpaid fee of £1.99. Pay now to reschedule: parcel-track-help.info/pay
clues: asks for a small fee; link is not the real courier website
explanation: Couriers don't text you for small fees. Check deliveries in the official app or website.

subject: bank
content: SECURITY ALERT: A new device has signed in to your bank account. If this wasn't you, verify your identity immediately at secure-bank-verify.com
clues: scary alert; urgent link to a look-alike website
explanation: Banks never ask you to 'verify' by clicking a link. Open your banking app yourself instead.

subject: family
content: Hi Mum, this is my new number, my phone broke. Can you save it and message me on WhatsApp? I need a small favour x
clues: unknown number claiming to be your child; 'small favour' (usually money)
explanation: Before helping, call your child on their OLD number or ask a question only they would know.

subject: tax
content: HMRC: You are eligible for a tax refund of £326.40. To claim, submit your details within 24 hours: gov-refund-claim.co
clues: tax office doesn't text refund links; deadline pressure
explanation: Government tax offices don't send refund links by text. Real government sites end in .gov.uk.

subject: job
content: Hi! We saw your CV online. Earn £300-£500 a day working from home, just 1 hour needed. Reply YES to learn more.
clues: huge pay for little work; you never applied
explanation: If a job pays a lot for almost nothing and finds YOU, it's almost always a scam.

subject: account
content: Your streaming subscription has been paused because we couldn't process your payment. Update your billing info to avoid losing access: stream-billing-update.net
clues: looks routine; link is not the service's real website
explanation: This looks routine, which makes it convincing. Always update payments inside the app, never through a text link.

subject: delivery
content: Royal Mail: Your parcel is being held at our depot. A redelivery can be booked here: royalmail.redelivery-uk.com Ref: RM8842
clues: real-sounding brand and reference number; the domain is not royalmail.com
explanation: Read links from right to left: this one belongs to 'redelivery-uk.com', not Royal Mail.

subject: delivery
content: Your parcel from BookNook will be delivered today between 13:00 and 15:00. Track in the courier app. No action needed.
clues: no payment request; says 'no action needed'
explanation: Real delivery updates just give information. Nothing to pay, nothing to click.

subject: appointment
content: Reminder: You have a dental appointment on Tuesday at 10:30 at Riverside Dental. Reply C to confirm or call the practice to change.
clues: matches an appointment you booked; no link
explanation: Reminders about something you booked yourself, with no links or payments, are normally safe.

subject: code
content: Your verification code is 482913. It expires in 10 minutes. Never share this code with anyone, including our staff.
clues: only a code; warns you never to share it
explanation: Genuine codes warn you not to share them. Only use one if YOU just asked for it.

subject: family
content: Hi love, landed safely! Bit tired. Will ring you tomorrow after work x
clues: from a saved contact; asks for nothing
explanation: A message from a saved contact that asks for nothing is very unlikely to be a scam.

subject: bank
content: Bank: You spent £42.10 at GreenGrocer Market. If you don't recognise this, open your banking app or call the number on the back of your card.
clues: tells you to use your app or card number, not a link
explanation: Real banks send you to their app or the number on your card, never a link in the message.

subject: delivery
content: We missed you! Your parcel is at the Corner Shop collection point. Bring this code: 7XQ2. Collect within 7 days.
clues: 'missed you' sounds like scams, but no fee and no link
explanation: This looks like a scam at first, but there's no money and no link. Real updates just tell you where to go.

subject: account
content: Your password was changed. If this was you, you can ignore this message. If not, open the app and go to Settings > Security.
clues: security alert, but sends you to the app, not a link
explanation: Real security alerts tell you to open the app yourself. Scam versions give you a link.

subject: appointment
content: City Health: your flu vaccine is due. Book at reception or through your usual GP app. Reply STOP to opt out.
clues: official-sounding, but nothing to click or pay
explanation: Health reminders that send you to your usual GP app or reception are safe to act on.

subject: phone-plan
content: Your monthly bill of £18.00 is ready. It will be collected by Direct Debit on the 5th. View it any time in your account.
clues: bill reminder with no link and no pressure
explanation: Normal bills tell you the amount and when it will be paid. They don't threaten you or demand action now.

subject: bank
content: URGENT: We've blocked a payment of £900 on your card. Please call us on the number on the back of your card.
clues: says URGENT like a scam, but asks you to use the number on your own card
explanation: A tricky one: 'URGENT' feels scammy, but calling the number on your own card is exactly the safe thing to do.

subject: family
content: Hey it's Sam from the running club, got your number from the group list. Are you coming Saturday?
clues: unknown number, but explains where they got it; asks for nothing
explanation: Unknown numbers aren't always scams. This one asks for nothing and you can check in the group chat.

subject: delivery
content: Courier: Your driver Alex is 5 stops away. Live tracking is in the app. Leave-safe instructions can be updated there.
clues: first name of driver and 'live tracking' look like phishing bait, but no link
explanation: Real couriers do share driver names. The safe sign: it sends you to the app, not to a link.

subject: code
content: Someone tried to sign in to your account from a new device. If this was you, enter code 551904. If not, no action needed — your account is safe.
clues: looks like a scary alert, but nothing to click and no request
explanation: Very tricky: alerts can be real. The key is that it doesn't ask you to click, call or pay anything.

subject: tax
content: Council Tax: your annual bill is now available. Log in to your council account through your local council website to view it.
clues: mentions tax and bills, but no link and no deadline
explanation: Tax messages make people nervous. This one is fine because it tells you to go to the website yourself.

subject: appointment
content: Library: The book you reserved is ready to collect at Central Library. We'll keep it for 7 days.
clues: something you asked for; no link, no payment
explanation: Messages about something you asked for, with no link and no payment, are usually genuine.
